description: vLLM observability organized by API reliability, user-visible latency, workload throughput, scheduler capacity, NVIDIA GPU hardware, prefix-cache efficiency, and MTP speculative decoding. HTTP failures remain separate from inference completion outcomes, and metrics with incompatible scales use independent panels or logarithmic axes.

panels.description: Whether Prometheus can scrape the vLLM metrics endpoint.
panels.title: vLLM

panels.description: OpenAI-compatible API requests per second across the selected endpoints.
panels.title: Request rate

panels.description: HTTP 4xx and 5xx responses as percentages of selected API requests. Client failures remain separate from the primary 5xx service reliability signal.
panels.title: HTTP error ratios

panels.description: 95th-percentile time from request arrival to the first generated token. This includes tokenization and queueing.
panels.title: P95 time to first token

panels.description: Generation tokens produced per second. Unlike request rate, this reflects actual decode work.
panels.title: Generation throughput

panels.description: Requests waiting for scheduler capacity or transient constraints. Sustained non-zero values indicate saturation.
panels.title: Waiting requests

panels.description: API traffic split by HTTP status class. Keep 4xx client failures separate from 5xx service failures.
panels.title: API request rate by status

panels.description: Finished inference requests by outcome. Length means the configured output limit was reached; abort normally means cancellation or disconnection, not an HTTP 5xx.
panels.title: Inference completion outcomes

panels.description: Time to first token percentiles. This is the primary responsiveness signal for streamed generation.
panels.title: Time to first token

panels.description: Per-request generation time normalized by output token count. This is more comparable across response lengths than end-to-end latency.
panels.title: Time per output token

panels.description: Distribution of gaps between streamed output tokens. Unlike per-request TPOT, ITL exposes token-level stalls and uneven streaming that averages can hide.
panels.title: Inter-token latency

panels.description: Time spent processing prompt tokens before decode begins. Interpret it with prompt size and prefix-cache hit rate.
panels.title: Prefill latency

panels.description: Time spent generating output tokens after prefill. It grows with response length; TPOT and inter-token latency are better normalized decode-speed signals.
panels.title: Decode latency

panels.description: End-to-end latency includes the complete generated output and varies strongly with response length. A logarithmic axis keeps median and tail percentiles visible when they differ by orders of magnitude.
panels.title: End-to-end request latency

panels.description: Logical prompt tokens admitted per second, including tokens served from prefix cache. This measures workload volume, not just GPU prefill computation.
panels.title: Prefill input throughput

panels.description: Prompt tokens actually computed per second after excluding local prefix-cache hits and externally transferred KV tokens. This is the GPU's effective prefill work rate.
panels.title: Prefill compute throughput

panels.description: Output tokens generated per second during decode. This is aggregate server throughput; TPOT and inter-token latency describe per-request responsiveness.
panels.title: Decode throughput

panels.description: Mean time spent waiting for scheduler admission, calculated from exact histogram sum and count. Kept with scheduler metrics because queueing diagnoses capacity pressure rather than model execution latency.
panels.title: Average request queue time

panels.description: Requests actively executing and waiting, with waiting requests split by scheduler reason when the running vLLM version exposes that metric.
panels.title: Scheduler requests

panels.description: Current KV-cache occupancy. Sustained high utilization, especially alongside waiting requests or preemptions, indicates capacity pressure.
panels.title: KV cache utilization

panels.description: Cumulative scheduler preemptions converted to a per-second rate. Sustained preemption usually accompanies KV-cache or scheduling pressure.
panels.title: Scheduler preemptions

panels.description: Current GPU graphics/core clock frequency reported by the NVIDIA driver.
panels.title: GPU core frequency

panels.description: Current GPU VRAM clock frequency reported by the NVIDIA driver.
panels.title: VRAM frequency

panels.description: Framebuffer memory in use as a percentage of total GPU VRAM.
panels.title: VRAM utilization

panels.description: Percentage of the collection interval during which one or more GPU kernels were executing.
panels.title: GPU compute utilization

panels.description: Current board power draw alongside the enforced power cap and the GPU's factory default power limit (TDP). Paimon currently enforces a 350 W cap.
panels.title: Power draw / TDP

panels.description: Share of queried prefix tokens served from the prefix cache over the selected rate interval. Interpret this against workload prefix reuse rather than as a capacity signal.
panels.title: Prefix cache hit rate

panels.description: Prefix tokens queried and reused per second. The gap between queried and hit tokens shows how much prompt work still requires computation.
panels.title: Prefix cache activity

panels.description: Share of MTP draft tokens accepted by the target model over the selected rate interval. Higher is better, but latency and generation throughput remain the outcome metrics.
panels.title: MTP acceptance rate

panels.description: Mean accepted sequence length per speculative draft, including the bonus target token. With three MTP draft tokens, the theoretical range is 1–4 tokens.
panels.title: Mean MTP acceptance length

panels.description: Unconditional acceptance probability for each MTP draft position. Later positions are accepted only when every earlier position was accepted, so the curves should decrease monotonically.
panels.title: Acceptance by MTP position
